design_decisions.D8: OWNER DECISION, 2026-09-06, recorded in kcl/PLAN.md §1: fpjson P0 = pure bash — handle model (document instance + parallel arrays) + windowed regex lexer; the awk accelerator stays in fpjson's own P8. Both July forks are hereby CLOSED; no further owner review gate before P1.
design_decisions.node_model: (B) ONE kklass instance per DOCUMENT; nodes are integer handles into six per-document globals: ${doc}_type (o/a/s/n/b/z), ${doc}_value (scalar payload), ${doc}_kids (SPACE-separated child id list), ${doc}_names (the node's own member name, indexed by the CHILD id — never a joined list, because JSON names may contain any byte incl. \x1f), ${doc}_parent, ${doc}_index (assoc, key '<parentId>:<name>' -> childId, unambiguous because the id is decimal up to the first ':'). Document scalars (root, nextid, count, opts, maxdepth, err) live in kklass's own state = ${doc}_data. Rejected: (A) instance per node — TDictionary.new ~1.2 ms x 10k nodes; (C) path-only API — O(depth) per access.
design_decisions.D8-1: Handles are MONOTONIC and never recycled; 0 = 'no node'. No free list: recycling an id makes a stale handle silently address a different node and bash has no cheap generation counter. Side benefit — atomic parse is a watermark unset (§5.2). Cost: ids grow with nodes ever allocated in a mutation-heavy document; doc.Clone into a fresh document compacts.
design_decisions.D8-2: Lexer window = 256 bytes, refill below 64, grow x4 for a token longer than the window. D8 named 2 KB as a planning figure; the measured sweep says 2 KB costs ~40% more on BOTH bashes because the per-token cost is one match plus one O(window) shift.
design_decisions.D8-3: Lexer form = HYBRID: sliding window + a first-byte `case` for the token kind, with the regex engine entered ONLY for strings and numbers. Punctuation and true/false/null (about half the tokens of a real payload) never touch it. Measured faster than the single all-kinds regex on both bashes.
design_decisions.D8-4: \u0000 is DROPPED, following FPC (jsonscanner.pp:365-369: with no pending high half S:='' and u1:=u2, so the escape contributes nothing) — NOT a parse error as the July draft said. FPC wins over the draft per the review rules, and bash cannot hold a NUL in a variable anyway.
design_decisions.D8-5: Max nesting depth default 512, settable, 0 = unlimited. FPC has NO depth guard anywhere in the four units — this is a documented ADDITION, not claimed parity.
design_decisions.D8-6: CompressedJSON and StrictEscaping are PER DOCUMENT, where FPC makes them class properties shared by every instance (fpjson.pp:150, :390). A process-wide switch is action at a distance in a shell.
design_decisions.parser_structure: Iterative explicit-stack state machine (st_node/st_type + a pending key); FPC's own parser is the same shape (jsonparser.pp:100-124). Atomic failure: Parse records state[nextid] as a watermark and on ANY error unsets every id from the watermark up across all six arrays and restores state[root]/state[count] — a failed parse leaves the document byte-identical.
design_decisions.numbers: STRING-PRESERVING: one number kind + int/float subtype tag; literals survive parse->serialize byte-exact (FPC collapses through Double, fpjson.pp:2031 — documented divergence, strictly MORE faithful to the input). AsInteger/AsInt64 go through kk.isInt (decimal, int64 range check); AsFloat through kk.isNum as a validated passthrough; arithmetic belongs to kcl/math. Pinned test rows: -0, 0, -0.0, 1E400, 1e-400, 1.5e3, 9223372036854775807, 9223372036854775808, 00, .5, 1., 1e, +1.
design_decisions.serialization: AsJSON is byte-parity with FPC's DEFAULT class-var state: ElementSeps=(', ',',') fpjson.pp:111 and ObjStartSeps/ObjEndSeps/ElementStart/SpacedQuoted/UnSpacedQuoted :606-611 -> `{ "a" : 1, "b" : 2 }`, `[1, 2]`, empty containers `{}`/`[]`. Escaping per StringToJSONString :881-917 over the set ['"','/','\\',#0..#31]: \\ \" \b \t \n \f \r, every other control char as UPPERCASE \u00XX (HexStr), '/' NOT escaped unless StrictEscaping, and #127 (DEL) NOT escaped at all. FormatJSON = the six TFormatOption values (:64-70) with DefaultIndentSize 2; sLineBreak is LF always (FPC would emit CRLF on Windows — documented divergence). Serializer is iterative like the parser.
design_decisions.unicode: Storage = raw UTF-8 bytes. The lexer pins `local LC_ALL=C` — VERIFIED on both bashes to switch ${#s}, ${s:i:n} AND [[ =~ ]] to byte mode and to be restored on return. This is a CORRECTNESS requirement, not an optimisation: a window boundary cuts multi-byte characters, and in a UTF-8 locale [[ =~ ]] fails to match an invalid byte sequence (measured both ways). printf '\uXXXX' is UNUSABLE inside that region — measured on both bashes, `printf -v v '\u00e9\u4e2d\U0001F600'` yields byte e9 followed by the LITERAL text for the other two — so UTF-8 is composed arithmetically from the code point, with surrogate pairs combined as cp = 0x10000 + ((hi-0xD800)<<10) + (lo-0xDC00). Lone surrogates are emitted as FPC emits them (3-byte CESU-8 via UTF8Encode of a single WideChar).
design_decisions.insertion_order: TJSONObject preserves insertion order (TFPHashObjectList, fpjson.pp:606; Names[i]/Items[i] walk it by index) — kept: _kids is an ordered id list, and serialisation and iteration follow it.
design_decisions.duplicate_keys: S1, pinned from the source. On Add: TJSONObject.DoAdd (fpjson.pp:3725-3741) raises EJSON 'Duplicate object member: "%s"' (:822) -> our rc 1 + RESULT='' + the same text in doc.LastError. On parse: jsonparser.pp:130-137 lets that exception out, so the parse FAILS; with joIgnoreDuplicates (:138-142) the later value is discarded and the FIRST wins. Default = FPC default = reject, with the offending key's position. On serialise: no policy needed — the model cannot hold a duplicate; a test asserts that rather than leaving it implicit.
design_decisions.findpath: S5, pinned from three impls. Object (fpjson.pp:3276-3307): empty path -> self; leading dots skipped (note the strict `P<L`); a segment runs to the next '.' or '['; an EMPTY segment returns Self and DISCARDS the rest — so a path starting with '[' against an object returns the object itself; otherwise Find(name) and the remainder keeps its separator. Array (:2512-2542): '[' must be first, P:=Pos(']'), the index is parsed only when P>2, must satisfy 0<=i<Count, remainder is everything after ']'. Scalar (:1489-1497): any non-empty path is a miss. GetPath = FindPath + SErrPathElementNotFound (:823, :1532) -> rc 1 + LastError. CONSEQUENCE reproduced deliberately: a member whose name contains '.' or '[' CANNOT be reached by a path; doc.Element is the way. DIVERGENCE: FPC parses the array index with StrToIntDef, which accepts $/0x/% prefixes; we accept what kk.isInt accepts (decimal with an optional sign).
design_decisions.error_contract: D2 exactly: rc 1 + RESULT='' + silence, one kk.debug line. rc 2 only for a malformed CALL (bad output-array name via kk._outName, non-identifier where an identifier is required, wrong arity). A non-integer handle is rc 1, not 2 — it is a value the caller may legitimately try, and it goes through kk.isInt FIRST because ${doc}_type[$h] would otherwise EXECUTE an injected command substitution. The positioned message stays reachable as DATA through doc.LastError ('line L col C: message'), so D2 and the usability requirement are both met. Position tracking never counts per byte: line/lineStart are updated only for chunks that can contain a newline, via nl=${chunk//[!$'\n']/}.

measurements.host: Windows 11 / MSYS2, bash 5.2.37 and 5.3.9, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 ambient
measurements.documents: generated under a scoped LC_ALL=C so both bashes get identical input: 2081 B / 797 tokens, 20355 B / 7637 tokens, 97385 B / 36221 tokens

window_sweep_20KB_ms.note: regex / hybrid / winbytes at each window size

measurements.gate: P0 gate (kcl/PLAN.md P10): 20 KB <= 1 s on 5.2.37 with the windowed lexer. PASS at 290 ms (5.2) / 251 ms (5.3) with the default 2048 window, 239 ms / 211 ms at the pinned 256. The probe asserts the gate itself and exits non-zero if it ever fails.
findings: The WINDOW is what buys the 5-24x, not the regex: a plain character scan inside a window is as fast as the all-in-one regex, and faster on 5.3.9. D8's windowed-regex lexer is adopted for correctness-per-line (one match yields the whole token and validates the number grammar), and the hybrid form recovers the speed.
The optimum window is 256 B, not the 2 KB named in D8 — the per-token cost includes an O(window) shift.
The naive string pattern "([^"\\]|\\.)*" backtracks catastrophically; the unrolled "[^"\\]*(\\.[^"\\]*)*" is mandatory.

local LC_ALL=C puts ${#s}, ${s:i:n} AND the [[ =~ ]] engine into byte mode on both bashes and is restored on return; in a UTF-8 locale a window that ends mid-character makes [[ =~ ]] FAIL TO MATCH, so the scoped C locale is a correctness requirement.
printf '\uXXXX' / '\U........' are unusable inside that C-locale region on both bashes (\u00e9 -> raw byte e9; \u4e2d and \U0001F600 left literal), which is why the UTF-8 encoder is arithmetic.

Teardown, 10k nodes: build 5 assoc arrays 78 ms (5.2) / 74 ms (5.3); build 5 indexed arrays 87 / 87; `unset -v` of all six arrays 8 / 4 ms. P6 target for doc.delete of a 10k-node document: <= 50 ms on both bashes.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE (cost an early mis-run): a `VAR=value` prefix on the msys->cygwin `bash.exe` invocation does NOT reach the child (the probe reported LC_ALL unset); `env VAR=value /c/bin/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe …` does. Use `env` when pinning a locale for the 5.3.9 runs.

out_of_scope.reason: One literal-preserving number kind + subtype tag; no Double roundtrip, no float engine. Documented divergence (strictly MORE faithful to the input text than FPC).
No streams in bash; ParseFile reads whole files. SAX-style is the P8 coproc's possible future, not v1.
Separate FPC units; CompareJSON noted as a possible later extra.
bash strings are UTF-8 bytes; one string kind.
No variants in bash; the AsXxx family covers it.
A TFPHashObjectList artefact; we have no such limit and do not fake one.
A Pascal callback type; a bash sort of an array node is a later extra, not v1.
bash language limit; \u0000 follows FPC and is dropped (D8-4), and ParseFile rejects a file that contains a real NUL.

open_questions.question: Dialect default. FPC's DefaultOptions=[joUTF8], i.e. joStrict is OFF: it accepts single-quoted strings (jsonscanner.pp:317), unquoted/identifier member names and case-insensitive TRUE/Null (:569-580), raw control characters inside strings (:396), leading zeros (:423), .5 and 1.e5 (:426,:440). The plan defaults to STRICT RFC 8259 and offers the lenient dialect via doc.Options.
open_questions.reason: silently accepting {name: .5} from an API is a bug amplifier; both dialects are implemented and tested either way, so switching the default is a one-line change.

open_questions.question: CompressedJSON / StrictEscaping scope: per document (D8-6) vs class-wide as in FPC (fpjson.pp:150, :390).
open_questions.reason: a process-wide switch is action at a distance in a shell; kklass static properties could reproduce FPC's shape if API-shape parity matters more.

open_questions.question: doc.ObjAdd returns the new child HANDLE; FPC's Add returns the insertion INDEX (fpjson.pp:3743).
open_questions.reason: the handle is what every other member consumes; the index is Count-1 / IndexOfName. One line either way.

execution_log.summary: PLAN.md rewritten in full (737 lines) against the FPC sources re-read at tag release_3_2_2 and against measurements taken here. The July draft's central perf assumption was wrong and is corrected: a whole-document ${s:i:1} scan is O(n^2) — 96 KB = 38.7 s on 5.2.37 — while the windowed hybrid lexer does 20 KB in 290 ms and 96 KB in 1.59 s. New deliverable bench/lexer_probe.sh runs four tokenizers over 2/20/96 KB on both bashes, cross-checks their token counts, sweeps the window size, self-tests six edge documents (5 KB string, escapes, astral UTF-8, whitespace, empty containers, deep nesting) and asserts the P0 gate itself. Decisions D8-1..D8-6 recorded. Gaps the review named are all closed in the plan: _parent, FindPath grammar for names with '.'/'[', duplicate-key policy on parse AND Add, max-depth default, error contract = D2 with doc.LastError as the data channel, AsJSON of control chars (uppercase \u00XX; DEL not escaped), the 10k teardown target, and the -0/1E400/int64 number rows. Three open questions (O1-O3) carry chosen defaults. NO unit code was written — this phase is planning plus one measurement script, by design.
